title: Class Components Core Check
description: Check your understanding of class syntax, state, lifecycle methods, this binding, and function component migration.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which method must a class component define to return UI?
questions.explanation: Class components return their UI from the render method.

questions.prompt: How should class component state usually be updated?

options.text: By assigning this.state directly after mount

questions.explanation: setState schedules state updates and tells React to render with the new state.

questions.prompt: Which are common class lifecycle methods? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Mount, update, and unmount work in class components is handled through lifecycle methods.

options.text: After the component is first rendered and committed
On every state update before render

questions.explanation: componentDidMount runs after the component has mounted.

questions.prompt: Class component render methods should be pure and avoid side effects.
questions.explanation: render should describe UI from props and state without causing external side effects.

questions.prompt: Why do class event handlers often need binding?

options.text: To make this refer to the component instance when the handler runs

questions.explanation: JavaScript method calls can lose this, so handlers need binding or arrow class fields.

questions.prompt: How does class setState handle object updates?

options.text: It shallowly merges the provided object into current state
It deeply clones every nested object

questions.explanation: Class setState merges top-level object keys, but nested data still requires immutable updates.

questions.prompt: Which hook commonly maps to side-effect lifecycle work in function components?
questions.explanation: useEffect covers many synchronization cases previously handled by lifecycle methods.
